<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916782_theRebbe_480" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916782_theRebbe_480__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar for Yud Shevat 5729.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S.</t>
    <t s="1">Yud Shevat,</t>
    <t s="2">5729</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Shechinah was originally in the lower realms, was removed through undesirable events, and was brought down again by seven tzaddikim, culminating in Moshe and the Mishkan, linking this to the inheritance of the land by tzaddikim.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"I have come to My garden, My sister, My bride"1,</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the hillula, brings in the maamar of the day of his passing, the day of his hillula2,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is stated in Midrash Rabbah</t>
    <t s="3">(in its place)</t>
    <t s="4">"to My garden" means "to My bridal chamber,"</t>
    <t s="5">to the place which was My essence originally,</t>
    <t s="6">that the primary dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="7">but through undesirable matters, the Shechinah departed from below to above, up to the seventh firmament,</t>
    <t s="8">and afterwards, seven tzaddikim arose and brought down the Shechinah from above to below,</t>
    <t s="9">until Moshe, who is the seventh, came,</t>
    <t s="10">and all sevenths are beloved3,</t>
    <t s="11">and he brought it down below to earth.</t>
    <t s="12">For this matter</t>
    <t s="13">(the drawing down and descent of the Shechinah below to earth)</t>
    <t s="14">was accomplished primarily4</t>
    <t s="15">through the Mishkan that Moshe made, as it is stated5</t>
    <t s="16">"And they shall make Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst."</t>
    <t s="17">And this is [the meaning of] "Tzaddikim will inherit the land and dwell forever upon it"6,</t>
    <t s="18">that this [matter] that tzaddikim</t>
    <t s="19">(and Your people7</t>
    <t s="20">are all tzaddikim8)</t>
    <t s="21">will inherit the land, which is the Garden of Eden, is because they cause to dwell</t>
    <t s="22">(draw down9)</t>
    <t s="23">the aspect of "He Who dwells forever, exalted and holy"10</t>
    <t s="24">so that it will be revealed below.</t>
    <t s="25">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="26">that according to what is stated in the maamar, that the explanation of "and dwell forever upon it" is that the tzaddikim draw down the aspect of "forever" so that it will be revealed below,</t>
    <t s="27">it is necessarily to say that "the land" in this verse is the physical land,</t>
    <t s="28">[for "upon it" refers to the "land" mentioned here],</t>
    <t s="29">and what is stated in the maamar, that "tzaddikim will inherit the land" is the Garden of Eden,</t>
    <t s="30">the intention in this is not for the world of souls as they are without bodies,</t>
    <t s="31">but rather for the Garden of Eden as it is in the physical land,</t>
    <t s="32">in which Adam HaRishon was</t>
    <t s="33">(in his physical body)</t>
    <t s="34">before the sin,</t>
    <t s="35">when the primary dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower realms.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the service of subjugation and transformation of the sitra achra draws down the light of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is equally in all worlds, transcending their infinite gradations.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that the service through which the drawing down of the primary Shechinah below was accomplished</t>
    <t s="3">(after it departed through the seven undesirable matters)</t>
    <t s="4">is the service of subjugation (itkafya) and transformation (ithapcha).</t>
    <t s="5">As the statement11</t>
    <t s="6">"When the sitra achra is subjugated, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all the worlds,"</t>
    <t s="7">[this refers to] the drawing down and revelation of the Essence (Atzmus) of Ein Sof, which is above any relation to worlds</t>
    <t s="8">[therefore this drawing down is called "elevation" (istalku),</t>
    <t s="9">because it is a revelation of the light that is in the aspect of transcendence12],</t>
    <t s="10">which is equally in all the worlds.</t>
    <t s="11">For in the worlds there is a multiplicity of levels without end13.</t>
    <t s="12">For this that is explained in many places, that there are two worlds,</t>
    <t s="13">as it is stated14</t>
    <t s="14">"from the world to the world,"</t>
    <t s="15">which are the hidden world and the revealed world15,</t>
    <t s="16">is in general terms16,</t>
    <t s="17">but in particular they are divided into four worlds Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah (ABiYA)</t>
    <t s="18">[And it can be said that this is what the maamar brings at the beginning of the matter from the Midrashic statement17</t>
    <t s="19">"He stretched out His right hand and created the heavens, He stretched out His left hand and created the earth,"</t>
    <t s="20">and afterwards he explains "the difference in the four worlds,"</t>
    <t s="21">for the totality of all worlds is divided into two general levels,</t>
    <t s="22">upper worlds</t>
    <t s="23">(heavens)</t>
    <t s="24">and lower worlds</t>
    <t s="25">(earth),</t>
    <t s="26">similar to the hidden world and the revealed world,</t>
    <t s="27">but in particular they are four worlds ABiYA],</t>
    <t s="28">and in even greater particularity, into a multiplicity of worlds without end.</t>
    <t s="29">And this is the novelty and superiority of this light, that it is "in all the worlds,"</t>
    <t s="30">for although there is a multiplicity of divisions in the worlds from the beginning of all levels until the end of all levels,</t>
    <t s="31">nevertheless, it is equally in all the worlds,</t>
    <t s="32">because it is above any relation to worlds.</t>
    <t s="33">And the drawing down of this light, which is equally in all the worlds, is through the service of subjugation (itkafya) and transformation (ithapcha).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
